title: observability-token-kv-logging-metrics-dashboard-alert-tuning-extended
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: improve token-level KV cache observability by adding detailed logging, enhancing metrics emitted by the serving runtime, and shipping an updated Grafana dashboard with tuned alerts. This PR consolidates three efforts: (1) add structured logging for KV cache hits/misses and eviction events to help debug degraded cache effectiveness, (2) expose additional Prometheus metrics for per-model token cost/latency breakdowns and KV cache contribution, and (3) publish a pre-baked Grafana dashboard and alert rule set with tuned thresholds for P99 latency, cache hit rate degradation, and token-cost spikes. Changes include new logging hooks in the runtime, a lightweight metrics shim to avoid high-cardinality pitfalls, a dashboard JSON export, and alert playbooks. Testing: unit tests for metrics emission and log formatting, integration test in perf-canary env showing expected metric rollups, and manual validation of dashboards in staging. Rollout plan: feature-flagged runtime changes, staged rollout to Dedicated clusters then Hosted, 72h monitoring window with auto-rollback on alert regressions. Related: ENG-5421 for KV cache improvements, SUP-3472 customer report that prompted additional logging. Checklist: - [x] Add structured KV cache logs - [x] Add and document new Prometheus metrics - [x] Dashboard JSON + dashboard provisioning automation - [x] Alert tuning and runbook updates - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Feature flag gated rollout

review_comments: Ravi Patel: Can we avoid adding model_id as a label on Prometheus metrics? Concerned about cardinality. Suggest using model_family instead.
Ava Martinez: Agreed on cardinality constraints; metrics use model_family and region as labels. We keep model_id only in structured logs to allow trace-level correlation.
Elena Gomez: Alert thresholds look reasonable but suggest adding a short delay window to reduce flapping during deploys.
Ava Martinez: Added 10m sliding window and a 5m cooldown on alert re-fires. Also added automatic suppress during canary rollout.
Marcus Liu: Verified staging perf-canary run, p99 latency shows expected small regression (<5%) and kv hit-rate increased after tuning.
release_notes: Improved token-level KV cache observability: structured logs, new token cost/latency metrics, updated Grafana dashboard, and tuned alerts. Feature-flagged rollout to Dedicated and Hosted. This improves debugging for cache regressions and gives teams a clearer cost/latency breakdown.
notes: Follow-up tasks: backfill dashboards for historical data in observability pipeline (ENG-5490), add ingestion filter to avoid sampling hot routes, and add an SDK example for dashboard linking from Console.
